paper_metadata.title: Quantum Risk Modeling: Redefining Actuarial Science with Quantum Algorithms

experiments.description: Quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo / quantum amplitude estimation for tail-risk probability estimation on simulated actuarial and financial risk data, benchmarked against classical Monte Carlo.

algorithm.variant: quantum amplitude estimation (QAE) / quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo

hyperparameters.iterations: small number of iterations vs millions for classical Monte Carlo

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Probability distributions are encoded into qubit states to estimate tail-risk probabilities and conditional expected values.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate tail-risk probability / conditional expected values / solvency probabilities with fewer samples than classical Monte Carlo.

problem_instance.description: Simulated actuarial data and publicly available financial risk benchmarks, including synthetic insurance claim data, catastrophe risk scenarios, and financial market loss distributions.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic insurance claim data, catastrophe risk scenarios, and financial market loss distributions; no further dataset identifiers, date ranges, or splits reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical preprocessing and transformation of actuarial data into quantum-representable forms; exact steps not specified.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared against classical Monte Carlo on accuracy, computational runtime, scalability, and convergence velocity; no number of runs or seeds reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data preprocessing, feature normalization, and encoding of actuarial variables into quantum-representable states.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical interpretation of quantum-estimated probabilities into actuarial risk measures such as solvency ratios, VaR, and stress-testing outputs.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation applied to tail-risk probability estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper states a quadratic speedup qualitatively; no problem size, qubit count, or statistically rigorous benchmark protocol reported.

speedup_claims.conditions: on simulated actuarial data and publicly available financial risk benchmarks
speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as an overall runtime reduction; exact runtime values, number of runs, and confidence intervals are not provided.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quadratic speedup over classical Monte Carlo is claimed qualitatively
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo requires millions of iterations for accuracy

experiments.description: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for portfolio risk diversification / reinsurance-style optimization in high-dimensional actuarial settings.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Optimization over high-dimensional actuarial decision variables; exact binary encoding not specified.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize risk exposure while maintaining solvency and regulatory constraints; portfolio diversification / reinsurance optimization.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraints are described qualitatively as solvency constraints and regulatory guidelines; no explicit penalty formulation reported.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio risk diversification and actuarial optimization on simulated financial/insurance risk data.

dataset_specification.description: Simulated actuarial data and publicly available financial risk benchmarks; no asset list or benchmark identifiers reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical preprocessing and transformation of actuarial data into quantum-usable form; details not specified.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared with classical linear programming on portfolio diversification efficiency and scalability; no repeated-run protocol reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical preprocessing of actuarial data before quantum optimization.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical validation and interpretation of QAOA outputs into actuarial decision measures.

speedup_claims.conditions: for high-dimensional actuarial optimization / portfolio risk diversification problems
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper only claims better efficiency in complex spaces; no numerical benchmark, runtime, or approximation-quality results are reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Polynomial speedups are claimed qualitatively for optimization tasks
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical optimization described as limited in high-dimensional non-linear problems

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical actuarial pipeline combining quantum encoding, quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo, QAOA, and quantum machine learning for risk modeling.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Actuarial variables are translated into qubits using amplitude encoding and angle encoding.
problem_formulation.objective_function: End-to-end risk modeling for actuarial prediction, simulation, and optimization.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hybrid classical validation and regulatory compliance checks; no explicit mathematical constraint formulation reported.

problem_instance.description: Mortality tables, claim frequencies, and financial market data used as actuarial inputs for a hybrid pipeline.

dataset_specification.description: Mortality tables, claim frequency records, and financial market data; no dataset names, sizes, or splits reported.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical data preprocessing, cleaning, feature normalization, and transformation into quantum-representable states.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Assessed on accuracy, computation-efficiency, and robustness under quantum noise; compared against classical actuarial records and classical simulation outcomes.

noise_model.noise_type: noise, decoherence, and limited qubit count mentioned qualitatively
noise_model.error_mitigation_method: classical post-processing to correct remaining error or hardware noise

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data acquisition, cleaning, normalization, feature selection, and encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Aggregation of quantum outputs into solvency ratios, VaR, stress-testing measures, and classical ML-based correction of residual noise.

speedup_claims.conditions: hybrid quantum-classical actuarial pipeline with quantum-enhanced Monte Carlo, QAOA, and QML
speedup_claims.caveats: No numerical speedup is reported for the full pipeline; only qualitative claims of improved scalability and computational efficiency are made.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Hybrid pipeline claimed to provide polynomial speedups in some tasks
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical preprocessing and simulation are described as computationally heavy
